dish: Smash burger, deviled eggs, house pastries (coffee-soaked tart cherry chocolate cookie)
w: Café-bakery-market a short walk from the Speedway, opened 2024 by ex-Milktooth chefs Josh Kline and Zoë Taylor — European-leaning dishes built on Indiana farm produce. Indianapolis Monthly Best Restaurants 2025.

dish: Cocktails with Hoosier brandies and Indiana persimmon; New Orleans-style seafood
w: Fountain Square cocktail bar-restaurant in the old Thunderbird space from Ben Davis grad Nick Detrich (New Orleans/London bar veteran) — Hoosier-lore cocktails, Gulf-seafood plates, fried-chicken-and-Champagne nights.

dish: Al pastor and carnitas on nixtamalized corn tortillas; the broccolini taco
address: 1060 N Capitol Ave, Suite 1-103 (Stutz courtyard), Indianapolis, IN
w: Counter-service taqueria tucked into the Stutz building courtyard (Esteban Rosas & Gabriel Sañudo) — fresh masa tortillas, rotating tacos, lunch only. Named Indiana's best hole-in-the-wall taco joint (Cheapism) and on a national top-100 taco list.

dish: Pistachio latte (house pistachio orgeat, rose water, lemon peel); currywurst croissant
address: 401 E Michigan St (The Athenaeum), Indianapolis, IN
w: Three-level café in the Athenaeum's old coat-check rooms — grand staircase, stained glass, German-leaning pastries; its pistachio latte is a cult order among Indy coffee people.

dish: German-style lagers and 15+ house beers with a walk-up kitchen in the beer garden
w: Family-run near-westside microbrewery on a site steeped in racing history, with a year-round beer garden — voted Indy's Best Brewery (FOX59, 2022) and named among the city's leading breweries by Axios.

dish: Hoppopotamus IPA
w: Dog-friendly brewery with its own dog park off South College Ave that gives 5% of profits to animal and wildlife groups; its Hoppopotamus IPA is on taps all over town. Indianapolis Monthly Best New Breweries.

dish: Workingman's Pilsner, Preacher's Daughter Amber Ale
w: The neighbourhood's own brewery just south of downtown — solid core lineup (Workingman's Pilsner, Preacher's Daughter Amber, Soul Ride IPA) plus inventive seasonals.

dish: Tiki rum cocktails, oysters, scratch ramen; fried shiitakes with black-vinegar honey
w: Irvington rum-and-oyster bar (2019) from the Warner brothers with Love Handle's Benedyks — woven walls, hanging plants, deep rum list, oysters and house ramen. Indianapolis Monthly Best Restaurants 2026; Imbibe's where-to-drink-in-Indianapolis pick.

dish: Spritzes and vermouth; house focaccia and scratch pasta
w: Fountain Square aperitivo bar and trattoria modelled on Rome's Monti district (from Bovaconti Coffee's Minda Balcius; chef Francesco Settanni) — vermouth-forward bar, focaccia, scratch pasta, gelato. Indianapolis Monthly Best Restaurants 2026.

dish: Falafel sandwich with beet slaw and lemon tahini; fresh pasta (blond puttanesca)
w: Lunch-only Mediterranean/North African/Arab-world kitchen and pasta market (chefs Erin Kem & Logan McMahan) that replaced Nicole-Taylor's in January 2025; evenings are chef's-table dinners. Indianapolis Monthly Best Restaurants 2025 & 2026.

dish: Hibiscus-flower tacos, pork carnitas tacos, tamales
w: Carlos Hutchinson's Mexican kitchen that grew from a tamale takeout window into a full restaurant — traditional carnitas beside slow-cooked hibiscus 'tacos de jamaica' and creative vegan plates. On Diners, Drive-Ins and Dives (2024) and ranked No. 41 on Yelp's 2025 top-100 US taco list.

dish: Arabian Peninsula (Yemeni) plates and its own bakery breads
w: International Marketplace restaurant-bakery cooking the food of the Arabian Peninsula — a stop on WRTV's tour of the 80-restaurant Lafayette Rd/38th St corridor and on Visit Indiana's International Marketplace guide.

dish: Pho with a light, pristine broth; made-to-order stir-fries and noodle dishes
w: Lafayette Road Vietnamese long applauded by Indy pho devotees — Indianapolis Monthly's 'Star Player' in its Top Five Phos, and first on WRTV's where-to-eat-pho list.

dish: Dark, deep pho; lemongrass chicken, rice-paper rolls, clay-pot dishes
w: International Marketplace Vietnamese with a fortified, dark-broth pho, curries and clay pots — some of Indy's best rice-paper rolls and lemongrass chicken per Indianapolis Monthly's Top Five Phos; on WRTV's pho list.

dish: Egg rolls and pho
w: Southeast-side Vietnamese counter on Emerson Ave — an Indianapolis Monthly 'Cheap Eats' pick and on WRTV's where-to-eat-pho list.

dish: Tropical tiki classics and house rum cocktails
w: High-end tiki bar (2018) in a former Marion County courthouse building — part bar, part museum, holding one of the largest collections of Papua New Guinea tribal art outside a museum. Imbibe's Indianapolis pick; World's 50 Best Discovery listing.

dish: Clarified milk punches
address: 1107 Prospect St (Fountain Square Theatre Building), Indianapolis, IN
w: Signless speakeasy lounge inside the rambling 1928 Fountain Square Theatre Building — leather sofas, dim light and top-notch cocktails (Imbibe; Indianapolis Monthly's pandemic-era cocktail-bar openings).

dish: Coffee bar plus local beer and cider, with in-store live sets
w: Fountain Square record shop that is also a bar, coffee counter and small live-music room — on Imbibe's where-to-drink list; IBJ covered its expansion with a kitchen.

dish: House-roasted Tinker coffee by day; beer, wine and low-ABV cocktails with shareables after 4 pm
w: Indy roaster Tinker Coffee's café in Butler-Tarkington's 1932 Station 16 firehouse (ex-Chalet) — the Market Street café menu in the morning, a casual dinner-and-drinks room from 4 pm.

dish: Fried green tomatoes with pesto and grilled corn; chocolate-chip bread pudding
w: Butler-Tarkington's neighbourhood bistro since 2001, five minutes from Butler's campus — Southern-leaning small plates and kicked-up comfort food; Indianapolis Monthly's pick for a pre-show dinner on the Illinois St strip.

dish: Cheap beer and Saturday Punk Rock Night (since 2000)
w: Butler-Tarkington dive that opened as a piano bar in 1935 (original floor, metalwork and back-bar mirror) — home of Punk Rock Night, the world's longest-running weekly punk showcase; 7,000+ acts since 2001.

dish: Philly cheesesteak on South Jersey Liscio's rolls; hoagies with Chilly Water beer
w: Kristina Mazza's Southeast-Pennsylvania sandwich shop (2015) sharing a roof with Chilly Water's Butler-Tarkington taproom — imported South Jersey bread, Pennsylvania Dutch meats and sides.

dish: Oaktoberfest (2016 Brewers' Cup gold, European Amber Lager)
address: 50 N Airport Pkwy, Suite L, Greenwood, IN 46143
w: Indiana's second-oldest craft brewery (1994) — a Greenwood brewpub with family room, two bars and patio; celebrated 30 years on 4 July 2024.

dish: Crispy lamb ribs with chimichurri; maple-bacon Brussels sprouts; house beers
w: Westfield's chef-driven brewpub (2018) — ex-Cerulean/Bluebeard chef Alan Sternberg, twice a James Beard Rising Chef nominee, runs the kitchen beside the Dikos family's house brews. Indianapolis Monthly Best Restaurants 2026.

dish: Duck bolognese; butternut squash ravioli; aperitivo hour
w: Mother-and-son (Diane & chef Nicholas Gattone) Northern Italian restaurant in Zionsville's Boone Village — seasonal menu, fresh pasta, aperitivo hour 3-5 pm. Indianapolis Monthly review and Best Restaurants 2026.

dish: Fresh pasta made in the open pasta shop
w: Carmel trattoria (2016) from Cinque Terre-born Andrea Melani, with a glass-walled pasta shop where you watch the day's pasta being made — reviewed by the IBJ and featured by Visit Hamilton County.

dish: 16-course omakase; nigiri with fish from Hokkaido and Toyosu
address: 1685 E 116th St, Suite 155 (The Corner), Carmel, IN
w: Upscale Japanese room at The Corner in Carmel (opened 13 Nov 2025) — omakase counter, nigiri, miso cod and soba, designed end-to-end by co-owner Kimmie Chang. Indianapolis Monthly Best Restaurants 2026.

dish: The Big Ugly — a one-pound fully loaded burger (Man v. Food challenge)
w: Carmel Arts & Design District burger joint whose one-pound 'Big Ugly' earned a Man v. Food challenge (Adam Richman tapped out on the third) and a wall of fame for finishers; house ice cream too.

dish: The Batali — Smoking Goose coppa, soppressata and capocollo with provolone and giardiniera
w: Chris Eley's butcher-and-charcuterie market in Herron-Morton Place, birthplace of Smoking Goose Meatery (2011); its Batali sandwich is one of Indianapolis Monthly's 25 Essential Eats and Bon Appétit ranked it among the top ten sandwich shops in the US.

dish: Modern boeuf bourguignon, duck cassoulet, beef tartare
address: InterContinental Indianapolis (2nd floor), steps from Monument Circle, Indianapolis, IN
w: French-leaning all-day dining room on the second floor of the InterContinental, a block off Monument Circle — 'an impressive, modern take on boeuf bourguignon, cassoulet, sophisticated beef tartare' (Indianapolis Monthly Best Restaurants 2026); Axios's pick among Indy's best new restaurants for Devour 2026.

dish: English-style house ales; pub fare in a converted auto-parts store
w: Indiana's first brewpub (opened 14 Nov 1990 by Englishman John Hill) and the state's oldest operating brewery — the place that spurred Indiana's craft-beer industry; 35th birthday in 2025.

dish: Feijoada (weekends), Sinaloa tacos, crawfish quesadilla, caipirinhas
w: Broad Ripple Latin kitchen from Cristiano Rodrigues (Brazil) and Elizabeth Fernandez (Mexico), named for their son — the Brazilian dishes are Rodrigues's mother's recipes, and she runs the kitchen. Indianapolis Monthly Best Restaurants 2024, 2025 and 2026; a second location opened on Mass Ave.

dish: Ancho-peach glazed pork medallions; barbacoa with cilantro-lime crema; sancocho amuse-bouche
w: SoBro New Latin restaurant from the Northside Social group in a converted video store — Caribbean, Cuban and Dominican-inflected seafood and sauced meats; rave reviews from both Indianapolis Monthly and the IBJ.

dish: Extra-crisp crust pies like the Slaughterhouse Five; weekend huevos rancheros pizza
w: Mick McGrath's Irvington pizzeria (2007) that helped revive the neighbourhood — extra-crisp crusts and offbeat combos; Thrillist named it Indiana's best pizzeria and Reader's Digest's state pick followed (FOX59).

dish: Brisket, fried catfish, fried chicken, candied yams, chicken and dumplings
address: 2621 Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. St, Indianapolis, IN
w: Family-run cafeteria-style barbecue and soul-food line (moved in 2024 from College Ave to a bigger MLK St space near Crown Hill) — on Diners, Drive-Ins and Dives in October 2024, aired a month after founder George Nelson Sr. died.

dish: Ceviche, paella, arroz con pollo, skirt steak — shared plates
w: Central and South American shared plates in a restored 1890s horse stable off Mass Ave — ranked No. 91 on Yelp's 2023 Top 100 US restaurants and among its top Midwest picks (as reported by Axios and WRTV; Yelp counted only as a popularity measure).

dish: Pour-overs of single origins such as the Peru Cajamarca (toffee notes); careful lattes
address: 201 S Capitol Ave, Suite 110, Indianapolis, IN 46225
w: Small-batch Indy roaster's airy downtown café directly across from the Convention Center — among the best places in town for a perfect pour-over (Indianapolis Monthly's coffee and roaster round-ups); Gen Con week is its busiest.

dish: Its own house-distilled spirits, poured in tasting-room cocktails
w: Fletcher Place micro-distillery — the first service-disabled, combat-veteran-owned artisan distillery in the US — with a tasting room pouring its own spirits; one of the openings that turned Fletcher Place into a food-and-drink district.

dish: Gratinée Carmichael (French onion soup), scallops provençal, roast duck chasseur
address: Hotel Carmichael, Carter Green (overlooking the Palladium gardens), Carmel, IN
w: Approachable French brasserie in Carmel's Hotel Carmichael (chef Joseph Hsu) with a patio over the Palladium gardens — classic technique, local ingredients; reviewed by Indianapolis Monthly and Current.

dish: Lowcountry crab cakes, shrimp and grits
address: W Main St (1907 bungalow, Carmel Arts & Design District), Carmel, IN
w: Savannah-to-Charleston Lowcountry cooking from Hoosier chef Christine Daniel in a 1907 white bungalow with a pergola patio in Carmel's Arts & Design District — reviewed by Indianapolis Monthly; Visit Hamilton County's pick for elevated comfort food.

dish: Prime rib roasts, steaks and house-made turduckens
w: Butler-Tarkington butcher counter opened by L.E. Kincaid in 1921 and family-run ever since (the Dugdales bought it from his grandson in 2015) — a century-old neighbourhood institution on the Illinois St strip.
